additionalDisclosedFinding.finding: RULE_REFERENCE's own IR type is CAPACITY (types.ts), which is NOT a member of MONEY_NUMBER_RATIO - so RULE_REFERENCE cannot compose arithmetically inside an ADD/SUM/SUBTRACT alongside MONEY-typed operands (S6's own original test design attempted this and correctly failed at the type-check layer, revealing the real, narrow rule rather than a test bug in the production sense). RULE_REFERENCE is designed to stand ALONE as an entire capacityExpression (referencing another rule's whole capacity, e.g. a refinancing basket capped at exactly a prior rule's own remaining room), not to participate as one addend among several MONEY-typed figures. The corrected S6 uses METRIC_REFERENCE (a real dollar figure, e.g. 'principal amount refinanced') for that shape instead, which is the domain-correct construct and composes cleanly (S6b separately confirms RULE_REFERENCE's own real, standalone use case still works). Not fixed as a production change - genuinely narrow, not disruptive to any real holdout claim, and consistent with the mission's own 'do not introduce schema migration unless truly unavoidable' discipline - disclosed here as a real, honest finding from the whole-agreement audit rather than silently worked around in the test.
